paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Jacob ran without a word, Laban chased him for seven days, and Laban came in swinging with talk of the great harm he could do. Then God stepped in the night before and said, "Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad." (Genesis 31:24) Nobody in that camp was in charge of how this ended except God.

Now look at Jacob. He says if the God of his father had not been with him, Laban would have sent him away empty-handed, and then he says, "But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands…" (Genesis 31:42) Twenty years of changed wages, heat by day, frost by night, and God saw every bit of it. I know a little about being stuck in the dark with nobody noticing, baker, so hear me: the work you do when nobody is watching is watched.

And that's why the mound matters. Laban says, "May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other." (Genesis 31:49) Two men who didn't trust each other were reminded that God sees what they do when nobody else is there. So bake like it, friend, because the One who sees is the One who sets the table. Jacob's story is NOT done, so keep your apron on.
